_purpose: Predefined, bounded PAPER_AUTONOMOUS risk policy. The bot executes eligible strategies WITHOUT per-trade or per-coin manual approval, but every entry/exit is validated against these hard limits by the independent risk layer (app/risk/policy.py + PaperAutonomous.confirm_trade_entry). This is autonomous execution inside a policy, not unrestricted trading. PAPER ONLY.
revised: 2026-10-21 rev3 (CONSERVATIVE $100 PAPER preset; BTC stake raised 10->15 after discovering Alpaca's ~$15 minimum order notional for BTC/USD made a $10 stake non-tradeable; owner approved the broker floor 2026-10-21)

authorization.paper_autonomous: APPROVED_BY_OWNER (directive 2026-10-21, CONSERVATIVE $100 preset): automatic BUY/SELL/HOLD/EXIT for eligible crypto in Alpaca PAPER without per-trade approval, sized for a $100 balance. Only the DAILY BTC executor is started first; the fast 5m alt executor stays configured but is not run until the $100 path is verified.

per_position.sizing: Quantity derived from the actual stop distance where applicable; stake is reduced further if the stop distance would breach max_planned_loss_usd.

portfolio.exposure_rule: effective cap = min(max_total_open_exposure_usd, max_total_exposure_pct_equity * current_paper_equity). On a $100 account this is min(55, 40) = $40 total open exposure; the $55 structural ceiling only lets validate_executors pass the worst-case whitelist sum (BTC $15 + 4 alts x $10 = $55).
portfolio.reported_buying_power_note: On the $100 paper account buying_power is ~$100. It is NOT the bound: the independent $40 (min of $50 fixed / 40%-equity) exposure cap is the real limit.

circuit_breakers.disclaimer: A loss limit does not guarantee an exact maximum loss; slippage, gaps, API failures and execution latency can produce worse results.

executors.note: Two DISJOINT PAPER order executors are CONFIGURED (CONSERVATIVE $100 preset, owner directive 2026-10-21). 'daily' = BTC baseline only (1d Z-score, stake $10) and is the only executor STARTED first. 'fast' = ETH/XRP/DOT/LINK (5m momentum, $10 each, max 3) stays configured but running=false until the $100 path is verified. Each Freqtrade process only sees its own trade DB, so the read-only monitor writes app/state/open_exposure.json and every confirm_trade_entry adds the OTHER executor's open stake before the exposure-cap check (fail-closed if the ledger is stale) — the $40 (min of $50 / 40%-equity) cap stays global, not per-process. Pair sets are disjoint. Structural worst case = BTC 15 + 4 alts x 10 = 55 <= fixed cap 55; positions 1 + 3 = 4 <= max_concurrent 4; runtime open exposure additionally bounded to ~$40 by the 40%-equity rule. NOTE: BTC stake is 15 (not 10) because Alpaca enforces a ~$15 minimum order notional on BTC/USD, so a $10 stake is silently un-fillable; alt stakes stay at 10 and will be re-based to each venue's true minimum before the fast executor is started.

fail_closed: Stale or unavailable market data / equity snapshot.
An unresolved order or open position already exists for the pair.
Any portfolio or per-position limit would be breached.
configurability: All amounts and percentages above are the source of truth and are validated at startup by app/scripts/preflight.py. Changing any limit requires a new owner-approved revision.
